- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; if price deviates >3σ from recent 18-day average, apply mean-reversion bias correction.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) often trigger model overconfidence; reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% if sentiment is high and price is rising.
- In 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag behind true price movements by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to align with 28–30 day true trend, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model often misinterprets momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to dampen volatility bias.
